overview.title: Astrobiology: The Search for Life in the Universe
overview.description: The scientific study of life's origins, evolution, distribution, and future in the universe
overview.keyQuestion: Are we alone in the universe?

exoplanets.signs: Oxygen, methane, water vapor in atmospheres

mars.evidence: Ancient river valleys, lakes, organic molecules

europa.evidence: Global subsurface ocean under ice shell
europa.potential: Hydrothermal vents like Earth's ocean floors

enceladus.evidence: Geysers shooting water into space from subsurface ocean

titan.uniqueFeature: Only moon with thick atmosphere and surface liquids
titan.composition: Lakes and seas of liquid methane

venus.cloudLayer: ~50-60 km altitude has Earth-like pressure and temperature

atmospheric.oxygen: O₂ - produced by photosynthesis on Earth
atmospheric.ozone: O₃ - shields life from UV radiation
atmospheric.methane: CH₄ - can be biological or geological
atmospheric.phosphine: PH₃ - strong biosignature if found with oxygen

surface.vegetation: Red edge - plants reflect near-infrared light

extremophiles.description: Life on Earth thrives in extreme conditions, expanding where we can look

thermophiles.implication: Life could exist on hot planets or near volcanic vents on ocean moons

psychrophiles.implication: Life possible in Martian ice or Europa's ocean

acidophiles.implication: Could survive in Venus's clouds or acidic exoplanet atmospheres

radioresistant.implication: Life could survive high radiation on Mars or Europa

barophiles.implication: Life in deep oceans of Europa, Enceladus

endoliths.implication: Subsurface life on Mars or other rocky worlds

siliconBased.challenges: Silicon bonds less versatile than carbon

ammoniaLife.concept: Ammonia as solvent instead of water

arsenicLife.potential: Arsenic substituting for phosphorus in DNA
arsenicLife.implication: Life might use different elements than we expect

drakeEquation.formula: N = R* × fp × ne × fl × fi × fc × L
drakeEquation.description: Estimates number of civilizations in Milky Way we might contact

factors.ne: Number of habitable planets per planetary system
factors.L: Length of time civilizations broadcast signals

drakeEquation.currentEstimates: Anywhere from 1 (us) to thousands of civilizations

fermiParadox.question: If life is common, where is everybody?
possibleAnswers: Life is extremely rare (Rare Earth hypothesis)
Intelligent life tends to destroy itself
We're looking in wrong places or wrong ways
We're first (we're early in universe's history)
Life is common but intelligence is rare
Great Filter: something prevents civilizations from reaching detectability

panspermia.concept: Life might spread between worlds on asteroids/comets
evidence: Microbes survive in space for years
Mars rocks ejected to Earth by impacts
panspermia.implications: Life on Earth might have originated on Mars or elsewhere
panspermia.directed: Advanced civilizations might seed life on other worlds

originOfLife.millerUrey: 1953 experiment showed organic molecules form from simple chemicals
originOfLife.hydrothermalVents: Life might have started at deep-sea vents
originOfLife.rnaWorld: RNA may have preceded DNA and proteins
originOfLife.clayHypothesis: Clay minerals catalyzed formation of organic molecules
originOfLife.electricSparks: Lightning in early atmosphere created building blocks
originOfLife.cosmicSeeding: Organic molecules delivered by comets and asteroids

methods: Radio telescope surveys scanning for artificial signals
Optical SETI looking for laser pulses
Searching for technosignatures in exoplanet data
seti.wowSignal: 1977 strong narrowband radio signal from Sagittarius - never repeated
seti.results: No confirmed detection of alien intelligence yet

currentMissions.perseverance: Searching for ancient life on Mars, caching samples for return
currentMissions.marsampleReturn: Will bring Mars rocks to Earth for detailed study
currentMissions.luvoir: Proposed telescope to directly image Earth-like exoplanets
